cosy-lesson.title: "They took memory cards from us and then made us pay for storage.": Nithya Shri

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Subscription – a regular payment made to receive a service.

p.em: Example: Paying a monthly subscription for digital cloud storage is very common now.

cosy-blockquote.p: Cloud – a network of remote servers on the internet used to store data.

p.em: Example: We store thousands of photos in the cloud without thinking about physical space.

cosy-blockquote.p: Physical – existing in a material form; tangible.

p.em: Example: While physical albums can be lost, digital photo libraries are secure but require storage fees.

cosy-blockquote.p: Storage – the space available for keeping data or physical objects.

p.em: Example: If you run out of phone storage, you must delete files or pay for more.

cosy-blockquote.p: Monetize – to earn money or generate revenue from an asset or service.

p.em: Example: Tech companies successfully monetize our private photos and personal records.

cosy-blockquote.p: Corporate – relating to a large company or business group.

p.em: Example: Corporate platforms control where and how we store our memories.

cosy-blockquote.p: Consumer – a person who purchases goods and services for personal use.

p.em: Example: The modern consumer pays countless monthly fees for basic electronic conveniences.

cosy-blockquote.p: Convenience – the state of being useful or suitable without difficulty.

p.em: Example: Digital convenience makes us forget that we don't actually own our files.

cosy-blockquote.p: Captive – kept in a space without a way to escape; dependent.

p.em: Example: Users are captive customers once all their life's photos are locked in one system.

cosy-blockquote.p: Asset – a useful or valuable quality, person, or thing.

p.em: Example: Personal memory has become a commercial asset for big data companies.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How has the rise of the subscription business model changed our concept of ownership?
★ How many monthly subscriptions do you currently pay for?

Is storing our memories in the cloud safer than keeping physical hard drives?
★ Do you worry about your cloud files disappearing or being hacked?

What do we lose when we replace physical books and photos with digital versions?
★ Do you prefer holding a physical book or reading on a screen?

Why do companies make us pay for additional storage rather than giving us expandable physical devices?
★ Have you ever run out of storage during an important event?

Is it ethical for technology giants to monetize our private lives and memories?
★ How do you feel about companies using your data to make a profit?

To what extent can we trust corporate databases to preserve our personal history?
★ Would you trust a corporate system with your most private journals?

How can the modern consumer protect their digital rights against tech monopolies?
★ Do you feel like a powerful consumer or a captive user in the digital age?

Why is the average user willing to sacrifice privacy and ownership for convenience?
★ Can you think of a convenience that you would gladly give up?

How do tech ecosystems ensure we remain captive customers by making migration difficult?
★ Have you ever felt locked into a specific phone brand or operating system?

When our attention and data are the product, does our memory become a corporate asset?
★ What is your most valuable non-material asset?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In a future where all physical databases are replaced by subscription models, personal records will belong to technology companies rather than ourselves. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you adapt if subscriptions became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

As cloud databases grow, future humans will completely lose the biological ability to remember simple facts. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your cloud memory?

Future educational systems will completely ban digital learning, returning to 100% Physical textbooks and handwriting. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with physical objects?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for digital storage compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of physical storage to children?

In the coming decades, if companies continue to monetize personal data, our most private thoughts will be sold as commercial commodities. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where personal data is fully monetized by corporations?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to resist corporate database control. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where corporate tech platforms own all personal data?

Future generations will look back at our current consumer habits with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about consumer rights to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true offline living a highly expensive luxury rather than a simple convenience. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees comfort at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's refusal to be a captive user of technology ecosystems. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope technology will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the mystery of what makes a memory a unique human asset. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of a memory asset, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: He have went to Paris → Correct: He has gone to Paris ((Present perfect third-person singular 'has' + past participle 'gone'.))

Incorrect: We discussed about the problem → Correct: We discussed the problem / had a discussion about the problem (('Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition, or use 'have a discussion about'.))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Use 'agree' directly as a verb rather than using it with the auxiliary 'am'.))
